title: Prevention of the first occurrence of neural-tube defects by periconceptional vitamin supplementation
followUp: One tablet daily from at least 1 month before conception until at least the second missed menstrual period, with ascertainment of the pregnancy outcome; trial begun in 1984, randomisation code broken at the end of 1991
population: Women planning a pregnancy, in most cases their first, in the Hungarian Family Planning Program; 4753 confirmed pregnancies, with outcome known for 2104 in the vitamin group and 2052 in the trace-element group
inKindSupport: Staff of Hoffmann-La Roche are thanked for supplying the supplements; the vitamin supplement was Elevit Pronatal (Hoffmann-La Roche).
result: Vitamin supplement with 12 vitamins including 0.8 mg folic acid, 4 minerals and 3 trace elements, against a trace-element supplement of copper, manganese, zinc and 7.5 mg vitamin C. Neural tube defects occurred in 0 of 2104 informative pregnancies in the vitamin group and 6 of 2052 in the trace-element group (P = 0.029); calculated from the counts, an absolute difference of 0.29 percentage points. Congenital malformations 13.3 against 22.9 per 1000 (P = 0.02). The authors could not exclude a synergistic effect of folic acid with the other vitamins.
